title: Common admissible modifications of two algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Open and closed immersions mean representable morphisms whose scheme base changes have the indicated property [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme; it is quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. Morphism properties use [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. For a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ on the small etale site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], write $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}T$ for the relative Proj of $\bigoplus_{d\geq0}\mathcal K^d$, constructed by etale descent of the ordinary scheme blowups [def-nagata-global-blowup] on affine etale charts. Finite type means locally generated by finitely many sections. Let $B$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space over $S$. Let $X_1,X_2,U$ be separated and of finite type over $B$, with open immersions $j_i:U\hookrightarrow X_i$ over $B$. There exist finite-type quasi-coherent ideals $\mathcal I_i\subseteq\mathcal O_{X_i}$ with $j_i^*\mathcal I_i=\mathcal O_U$, an algebraic space $W$ separated and of finite type over $B$, and open immersions $e_i:X_i^{\prime}=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I_i}X_i\hookrightarrow W$ over $B$. If $p_i:X_i^{\prime}\to X_i$ are the blowup maps, there are open immersions $s_i:U\hookrightarrow X_i^{\prime}$ identifying $U$ with $p_i^{-1}(j_i(U))$, such that $p_i s_i=j_i$ and $e_1s_1=e_2s_2$. No density of $U$ is required.

source.place: Tag 088Q (lemma-find-common-blowups); U-admissible centres as defined in spaces-divisors.tex Tag 086B (definition-admissible-blowup).

proof.text: First record the finiteness conditions. Every separated finite-type $B$-space $A$ is qcqs: finite type includes quasi-compactness by [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties], so pulling back along the identity of the quasi-compact base gives quasi-compactness of $A$. Its relative diagonal is closed, hence quasi-compact on scheme tests; [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-source-products] then gives absolute quasi-separatedness. Apply this to $U,X_1,X_2$. By [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence], the $j_i$ are quasi-compact. Put $P=X_1\times_BX_2$; it is qcqs by [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-source-products]. Its projections are finite type by the base-change clause of [lem-sfb-space-four-property-fppf-descent], and separated by [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition]. Their compositions to $B$ are finite type and separated by [lem-sfb-space-finite-type-composition, lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition]. The first argument will also establish qcqs for each separated finite-type $B$-space constructed below. Here and below an $S$-space can be viewed over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ when applying the absolute qcqs statement.

source.place: Tag 088Q (lemma-find-common-blowups), opening paragraph and formation of the product

proof.text: The map $u=(j_1,j_2):U\to P$ is a partial section of the separated projection $P\to X_1$ over the quasi-compact open $j_1:U\hookrightarrow X_1$. By [lem-sfb-space-partial-section-schematic-image] it has a smallest closed image $C\hookrightarrow P$, and the projection $p_1:C\to X_1$ is an isomorphism over $U$. Apply the same lemma to $P\to X_2$ and $j_2$. It gives the same $C$: each of the two smallest closed subspaces contains $u$ and so factors through the other. Thus $p_2:C\to X_2$ is also an isomorphism over $U$. By [lem-sfb-space-closed-subspace-proper], $C\to P$ is proper, hence finite type and separated. Compose with the projections and with $P\to B$, using [lem-sfb-space-finite-type-composition, lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition]. The resulting $p_i$ are finite type and separated, and $C$ is separated of finite type over $B$, hence qcqs by Step 1.

source.place: Tag 088Q (lemma-find-common-blowups), second paragraph, schematic image and its two projections

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-zariski-after-admissible-blowup] to $p_i:C\to X_i$ and $j_i(U)$. Its hypotheses hold by Steps 1 and 2: $X_i$ is qcqs, $U$ is quasi-compact, and $p_i$ is separated, of finite type and an isomorphism over $U$. Obtain finite-type ideals $\mathcal I_i\subseteq\mathcal O_{X_i}$, unit on $U$, spaces $A_i=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I_i}X_i$, and open immersions $$C_i=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K_i}C\hookrightarrow A_i,\qquad \mathcal K_i=\mathcal I_i\mathcal O_C.$$ These immersions commute with the maps to $X_i$ and restrict to the identity on $U$. Blowup maps are proper by [lem-sfb-space-blowup-chart-properties]. Thus $A_i\to B$ is separated and finite type by [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition, lem-sfb-space-finite-type-composition], and $A_i$ is qcqs by Step 1. Pullbacks of finite-type ideals are finite type: local generators of $\mathcal I_i$ pull back to generators of $\mathcal K_i$. Both $\mathcal K_i$ restrict to the unit ideal on the common $U\subset C$.

source.place: Tag 088Q (lemma-find-common-blowups), second paragraph, open strict transforms

proof.text: Set $T=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K_1\mathcal K_2}C$. The product ideal is finite type, with local generators the products of generators of the factors. By [lem-sfb-space-blowup-product-ideal-comparison], there are maps $r_i:T\to C_i$ identifying $T$ with the blowup of $C_i$ in the pullback of $\mathcal K_{3-i}$. These ideals are finite type and unit on $U$, so the $r_i$ are $U$-admissible blowups. All these maps commute over $C$ and agree with the identity on its open $U$. The spaces $C_i$ and $T$ are quasi-compact since their blowup maps to qc $C$ are proper and therefore quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-space-blowup-chart-properties]; they are quasi-separated by [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-source-products], since those proper maps are separated. For each blowup, its centre ideal is unit on $U$, so $U$ lies in the complement of its zero subspace. The open-restriction and complement clauses of [lem-sfb-space-blowup-chart-properties] therefore identify its inverse image of $U$ with $U$. These restrictions are along open immersions, within the flat-base-change hypothesis of that statement.

For each $i$, apply [lem-sfb-space-extend-admissible-blowup] with ambient space $A_i$, opens $U\subseteq C_i\subseteq A_i$, and the blowup $r_i:T\to C_i$. The ambient space is qcqs by Step 3, while $U,C_i$ are quasi-compact by Steps 1 and 4. The centre is disjoint from $U$ by Step 4. We obtain a $U$-admissible blowup $b_i:D_i\to A_i$ whose inverse image of $C_i$ is isomorphic over $C_i$ to $T$. Let $t_i:T\hookrightarrow D_i$ be the resulting open immersion. The square with $r_i$, $b_i$ and $C_i\hookrightarrow A_i$ is cartesian and commutative; in particular the two embeddings of $U$ agree with the one inherited from $T$. The maps $b_i$ are proper by [lem-sfb-space-blowup-chart-properties], so $D_i\to B$ is finite type and separated by [lem-sfb-space-finite-type-composition, lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition].

source.place: Tag 088Q (lemma-find-common-blowups), extension of the two blowups from the open strict transforms

proof.text: The composite $D_i\to A_i\to X_i$ is one $U$-admissible blowup by [lem-sfb-space-compose-admissible-blowups]: $X_i$ is qcqs, $U$ is quasi-compact, and both centres are finite type and unit on their identified copies of $U$. Thus there are finite-type ideals $\mathcal L_i\subseteq\mathcal O_{X_i}$, unit on $U$, and isomorphisms over $X_i$ $$D_i\cong\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal L_i}X_i$$ which restrict to the identity on $U$. Keep these isomorphisms for the final transport of the open embeddings.

source.place: Tag 088Q (lemma-find-common-blowups), last sentence, composition of admissible blowups

proof.text: Put $R=D_1\times_BD_2$ and $q=(t_1,t_2):T\to R$. The composite $T\to C\hookrightarrow P$ is proper: the first map is a finite-type-ideal blowup by [lem-sfb-space-blowup-chart-properties], the second is proper by [lem-sfb-space-closed-subspace-proper], and [lem-sfb-space-proper-composition] composes them. The map $R\to P=X_1\times_BX_2$ is separated: factor it as $D_1\times_BD_2\to X_1\times_BD_2\to P$; the factors are base changes of the separated blowups $D_i\to X_i$ of Step 6, so [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition] applies to both factors and their composition. The commutativity in Step 5 makes $(R\to P)q$ equal to $T\to C\to P$. By [lem-sfb-space-proper-cancellation], $q$ is proper.

source.place: Tag 088Q (lemma-find-common-blowups), properness of the comparison into the product

proof.text: The map $q$ is an immersion. Indeed its factorization $$T\xrightarrow{(\mathrm{id},t_2)}T\times_BD_2\xrightarrow{t_1\times\mathrm{id}}D_1\times_BD_2$$ is a closed immersion followed by an open immersion. The first arrow is the pullback of the closed diagonal of the separated map $D_2\to B$; the second is the pullback of the open immersion $t_1$. These are representable tests of [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]: quotient ring maps remain surjective under tensor product, and inverse images of open subschemes are open subschemes. For every scheme mapping to $R$, [lem-sfb-space-immersion-affine-tests] makes the source of the base-changed immersion a scheme. By [lem-sfb-space-proper-base-change] this scheme immersion is proper. Apply the scheme theorem [lem-weil-pbc-proper-immersion-closed] to each test: it is a closed immersion. This is exactly the representable closed-immersion condition, so $q$ is a closed immersion of algebraic spaces.

source.place: Tag 088Q (lemma-find-common-blowups), comparison is a closed immersion, with the scheme-test argument made explicit

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-glue-two-opens] to $t_i:T\hookrightarrow D_i$ over $B$. Obtain $e_i:D_i\hookrightarrow W$ over $B$, covering $W$, whose intersection is exactly $T$ with its two specified inclusions. The map $W\to B$ is locally of finite type: refine any etale scheme chart of $W$ by the inverse images of the opens $D_i$, and apply the source-locality of locally finite type in [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties] to these scheme opens. For every quasi-compact scheme $V\to B$, the space $W\times_BV$ is the union of the two quasi-compact open spaces $D_i\times_BV$, since $D_i\to B$ is finite type. A finite union of quasi-compact subspaces is quasi-compact (restrict an open cover to each and combine the two finite subcovers). Hence $W\to B$ is quasi-compact and therefore finite type by [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties].

source.place: Tag 088Q (lemma-find-common-blowups), gluing paragraph, existence and finite type of the glued space

proof.text: To prove $W\to B$ separated, test its diagonal on the four opens $e_i(D_i)\times_Be_j(D_j)$ of $W\times_BW$. On a diagonal part $i=j$, the pullback is $D_i\to D_i\times_BD_i$, which is closed since $D_i\to B$ is separated. On the two mixed parts the pullbacks are $q:T\to D_1\times_BD_2$ and its factor-swapped version, closed by Step 8. Refine these four open parts by scheme etale atlases. On each such scheme the base change of the diagonal is a closed immersion. By [lem-sfb-space-closed-immersion-atlas-locality] the diagonal is representable by closed immersions, so $W\to B$ is separated by [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. The off-diagonal fibre product is $T$, not merely the original $U$; this is why the product modification was needed.

source.place: Tag 088Q (lemma-find-common-blowups), footnote, four open parts of the relative diagonal

proof.text: Use the isomorphisms of Step 6 to view the $e_i$ as open immersions $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal L_i}X_i\hookrightarrow W$. Since $\mathcal L_i$ is unit on $j_i(U)$, this open is contained in $X_i\setminus V(\mathcal L_i)$. Restrict the complement isomorphism of [lem-sfb-space-blowup-chart-properties] to $j_i(U)$, giving its inverse open immersion $s_i:U\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal L_i}X_i$ and $p_is_i=j_i$. Step 4 gives a single copy of $U$ inside $T$, and Step 5 identifies its images with these canonical copies in $D_i$. The equality $e_1t_1=e_2t_2$ from [lem-sfb-space-glue-two-opens], restricted to that $U$, therefore gives $e_1s_1=e_2s_2$. Rename $\mathcal L_i$ as the ideals in the statement. No step assumed density of $U$; even $U=\varnothing$ is permitted.

source.place: Tag 088Q (lemma-find-common-blowups), final assembly and the canonical copies of the common open
